meta.macro_enhancement_note: Additional public RBA time series were integrated for model enhancement and macro/property research. They use latest revised history plus explicit release-lag metadata; they are not a true vintage database.
meta.research_foundations_note: Long-run prices, debt service, construction and population use latest revised public history. Publication lags and documented definition breaks must be enforced in backtests.
meta.housing_conditions_note: Ten additional public series cover borrower risk composition, buyer composition, rents, transaction turnover, dwelling stock and capital-city population growth.

home_value_index_mom.label: Home value growth, month-on-month
home_value_index_mom.definition: Monthly percentage change in the residential property price index.
home_value_index_mom.usage: Use it to identify short-run price momentum and early turning points before annual growth rates respond.
home_value_index_mom.housing_market_link: Positive readings indicate rising dwelling values; persistent acceleration can signal stronger demand relative to available supply.
home_value_index_mom.status_note: Subscription-dependent source for full monthly maintenance workflow. Keep as optional overlay while core monitoring uses public ABS/RBA series.

building_approvals_total_dwellings.label: Total dwellings approved (seasonally adjusted)
building_approvals_total_dwellings.definition: Number of dwelling units approved for construction, adjusted for recurring seasonal patterns.
building_approvals_total_dwellings.usage: Use it as a leading indicator of the residential construction pipeline, while allowing for projects that are delayed or never commence.
building_approvals_total_dwellings.housing_market_link: A sustained rise can add future housing supply and ease shortages; weak approvals can prolong supply constraints and housing-cost pressure.
building_approvals_total_dwellings.status_note: Latest parsed ABS seasonally adjusted dwelling approvals value is 18328.

building_approvals_total_dwellings_state.label: Dwelling approvals (Australia total; state proxies for cities)
building_approvals_total_dwellings_state.definition: Seasonally adjusted dwelling approvals: the National view is the Australia total, while Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth display NSW, Victoria, Queensland and WA respectively.
building_approvals_total_dwellings_state.usage: Use the National view for the aggregate construction pipeline and the city tabs for directional state comparisons; the city-labelled observations are not capital-city-only counts.
building_approvals_total_dwellings_state.housing_market_link: Approvals lead potential new supply, but not every approval commences and state totals can differ materially from capital-city conditions.
building_approvals_total_dwellings_state.status_note: National is the Australia total. City labels are state proxies: Sydney→NSW, Melbourne→VIC, Brisbane→QLD, Perth→WA.

cash_rate.label: RBA cash rate target
cash_rate.definition: The Reserve Bank of Australia's target for the overnight cash rate.
cash_rate.usage: Use it as the primary signal of monetary-policy stance and the direction of economy-wide borrowing costs.
cash_rate.housing_market_link: Cash-rate changes flow into mortgage pricing, borrowing capacity and repayments, affecting buyer demand, refinancing stress and property values.
cash_rate.status_note: Latest parsed RBA cash rate target is 4.35%.

housing_lending_rate_owner_occupier_vari.label: Housing lending rate (owner-occupier variable, all institutions)
housing_lending_rate_owner_occupier_vari.definition: Average variable interest rate on outstanding owner-occupier housing loans across lending institutions.
housing_lending_rate_owner_occupier_vari.usage: Use it to track the financing cost households are actually carrying, rather than relying only on the policy rate.
housing_lending_rate_owner_occupier_vari.housing_market_link: Higher mortgage rates reduce serviceability and purchasing power; lower rates can support transaction volumes and prices.
housing_lending_rate_owner_occupier_vari.status_note: Latest parsed RBA F6 owner-occupier outstanding variable housing lending rate (all institutions) is 6.3%.

unemployment_rate.label: Unemployment rate, seasonally adjusted
unemployment_rate.definition: Share of the labour force that is without work, available to work and actively seeking employment.
unemployment_rate.usage: Use it to assess labour-market slack, household income security and cyclical downside risk.
unemployment_rate.housing_market_link: Rising unemployment can weaken buyer demand and increase arrears or forced-sale risk; low unemployment generally supports repayments and housing demand.
unemployment_rate.status_note: Latest parsed ABS seasonally adjusted unemployment rate is 4.4%.

employed_people.label: Employed people, seasonally adjusted
employed_people.definition: Total number of employed people, seasonally adjusted and reported in thousands.
employed_people.usage: Use it alongside unemployment to distinguish genuine job creation from changes in labour-force participation.
employed_people.housing_market_link: Employment growth supports household formation, mortgage capacity and rental demand, particularly where jobs attract interstate or overseas migration.
employed_people.status_note: Latest parsed ABS seasonally adjusted employed people is 14823.3 ('000 persons).

cpi_trimmed_mean_yoy.label: Trimmed mean inflation, year-on-year
cpi_trimmed_mean_yoy.definition: Underlying annual inflation measure that removes the largest price rises and falls each period.
cpi_trimmed_mean_yoy.usage: Use it to judge persistent inflation pressure and the likely direction of RBA policy beyond volatile headline movements.
cpi_trimmed_mean_yoy.housing_market_link: Persistent underlying inflation can keep interest rates higher for longer, while also feeding construction, maintenance and rental costs.
cpi_trimmed_mean_yoy.status_note: Full available RBA G1 quarterly trimmed mean inflation history joined to the ABS complete monthly CPI publication at its first available recent observation.
cpi_trimmed_mean_yoy.methodology_note: Quarterly RBA G1 history is joined to the ABS complete monthly CPI series. Treat the frequency transition as a documented series break when reading cycles.

cpi_headline_yoy.label: Headline CPI inflation, year-on-year
cpi_headline_yoy.definition: Annual percentage change in the price of the household consumption basket measured by the Consumer Price Index.
cpi_headline_yoy.usage: Use it to track cost-of-living pressure, real household income and the broad inflation environment.
cpi_headline_yoy.housing_market_link: High inflation can squeeze deposit saving and repayment capacity, lift building costs and prompt tighter monetary policy that weighs on housing demand.
cpi_headline_yoy.status_note: Full available RBA G1 quarterly annual inflation history joined to the ABS complete monthly CPI publication at its first available recent observation.
cpi_headline_yoy.methodology_note: Quarterly RBA G1 history is joined to the ABS complete monthly CPI series. Treat the frequency transition as a documented series break when reading cycles.

lending_new_loan_commitments_dwellings_q.label: New loan commitments for dwellings, quarter-on-quarter
lending_new_loan_commitments_dwellings_q.definition: Quarterly percentage change in the seasonally adjusted number of new dwelling loan commitments.
lending_new_loan_commitments_dwellings_q.usage: Use it as a short-run momentum measure for funded housing demand; refer to the level series to distinguish growth from scale.
lending_new_loan_commitments_dwellings_q.housing_market_link: Accelerating commitments often accompany stronger turnover and buyer competition; contraction can foreshadow softer transactions and price momentum.
lending_new_loan_commitments_dwellings_q.status_note: Quarter-on-quarter change calculated from the ABS seasonally adjusted total number of new dwelling loan commitments; comparable total series begins in September quarter 2019.

vacancy_rate.label: Rental vacancy rate
vacancy_rate.definition: Percentage of the rental dwelling stock that is advertised as vacant or otherwise available for lease.
vacancy_rate.usage: Use it to measure rental-market tightness and the balance between available properties and tenant demand.
vacancy_rate.housing_market_link: Low vacancy rates tend to support faster rent growth and investor returns, while high vacancy rates indicate more tenant choice and weaker rental pressure.
vacancy_rate.status_note: Public headline figures available, but collection is still manual. Next step is adding repeatable monthly extraction for national and key capitals.

lending_new_loan_commitments_dwellings_n.label: New dwelling loan commitments (number)
lending_new_loan_commitments_dwellings_n.definition: Number of borrower-accepted new dwelling loan commitments, seasonally adjusted and excluding refinancing.
lending_new_loan_commitments_dwellings_n.usage: Use it to track the volume of financed housing transactions without the direct effect of changing dwelling prices or average loan sizes.
lending_new_loan_commitments_dwellings_n.housing_market_link: Rising commitments generally signal stronger funded buyer demand and can lead settlement and turnover activity.
lending_new_loan_commitments_dwellings_n.status_note: ABS seasonally adjusted total number of borrower-accepted new dwelling loan commitments; excludes refinancing and the comparable total series begins in September quarter 2019.

lending_new_loan_commitments_dwellings_v.label: New dwelling loan commitments (value)
lending_new_loan_commitments_dwellings_v.definition: Dollar value of borrower-accepted new dwelling loan commitments, seasonally adjusted and excluding refinancing.
lending_new_loan_commitments_dwellings_v.usage: Use it to measure the flow of new housing credit, while recognising that it reflects both transaction volumes and average loan size.
lending_new_loan_commitments_dwellings_v.housing_market_link: Credit-flow growth can support purchasing capacity and prices; divergence from commitment counts often reflects changing prices or borrower mix.
lending_new_loan_commitments_dwellings_v.status_note: ABS seasonally adjusted dollar value of borrower-accepted new dwelling loan commitments; excludes refinancing.

asx_200.label: S&P/ASX 200
asx_200.usage: Use it as a broad Australian risk-sentiment and listed-economy indicator.
asx_200.housing_market_link: Equity strength can accompany improving confidence and wealth, but the index is not a direct housing-price measure.
asx_200.status_note: Monthly closing index level retrieved via Yahoo Finance; latest observation is 2026-08.
asx_200.methodology_note: Monthly close; price-return index unless otherwise stated. Values may be revised by the data provider.

sp_500.label: S&P 500
sp_500.usage: Use it to track global risk appetite and US financial conditions.
sp_500.housing_market_link: Large global market moves can affect Australian funding conditions, confidence and household portfolios.
sp_500.status_note: Monthly closing index level retrieved via Yahoo Finance; latest observation is 2026-08.
sp_500.methodology_note: Monthly close; price-return index unless otherwise stated. Values may be revised by the data provider.

msci_acwi.label: MSCI ACWI (USD, price return)
msci_acwi.definition: Global developed and emerging-market equity performance in US dollars.
msci_acwi.usage: Use it as a broad global risk-appetite benchmark.
msci_acwi.housing_market_link: Global risk cycles can influence capital flows, funding costs and Australian household wealth.
msci_acwi.status_note: Monthly closing index level retrieved via Yahoo Finance; latest observation is 2026-08.
msci_acwi.methodology_note: Monthly close; price-return index unless otherwise stated. Values may be revised by the data provider.

asx_200_real_estate.label: S&P/ASX 200 Real Estate Index
asx_200_real_estate.definition: Price-return index for S&P/ASX 200 companies classified in the GICS real-estate sector.
asx_200_real_estate.usage: Use it to monitor listed-market expectations for Australian real-estate businesses.
asx_200_real_estate.housing_market_link: It is a liquid sentiment indicator, but includes commercial property and does not directly measure dwelling values.
asx_200_real_estate.status_note: Monthly closing index level retrieved via Yahoo Finance; latest observation is 2026-08.
asx_200_real_estate.methodology_note: Monthly close; price-return index unless otherwise stated. Values may be revised by the data provider.

asx_200_areit.label: S&P/ASX 200 A-REIT Index
asx_200_areit.definition: Price-return index for listed vehicles classified as Australian real-estate investment trusts.
asx_200_areit.usage: Use it to track listed property valuations and sensitivity to bond yields and funding costs.
asx_200_areit.housing_market_link: A-REIT performance is mostly commercial-property exposure and should not be read as a residential-price index.
asx_200_areit.status_note: Monthly closing index level retrieved via Yahoo Finance; latest observation is 2026-08.
asx_200_areit.methodology_note: Monthly close; price-return index unless otherwise stated. Values may be revised by the data provider.

us_treasury_3y.label: US Treasury 3-year yield
us_treasury_3y.usage: Use it to monitor medium-term US policy and growth expectations.
us_treasury_3y.housing_market_link: US yields influence global funding costs and can flow through to Australian wholesale funding and mortgage pricing.
us_treasury_3y.source: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED DGS3)
us_treasury_3y.status_note: Last available daily FRED observation in each month; latest month-end value is 4.26%.

us_treasury_10y.label: US Treasury 10-year yield
us_treasury_10y.usage: Use it as a global long-term discount-rate and inflation-expectations indicator.
us_treasury_10y.housing_market_link: Higher global long yields can pressure bank funding, fixed mortgage rates and listed property valuations.
us_treasury_10y.source: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED DGS10)
us_treasury_10y.status_note: Last available daily FRED observation in each month; latest month-end value is 4.71%.

wage_growth_private_yoy.label: Private-sector wage growth, year-on-year
wage_growth_private_yoy.definition: Annual growth in private-sector hourly rates of pay excluding bonuses, seasonally adjusted.
wage_growth_private_yoy.usage: Use it to assess household purchasing-power growth and labour-cost pressure in the private economy.
wage_growth_private_yoy.housing_market_link: Income growth supports borrowing capacity and repayments, while persistent wage pressure can also keep interest rates higher.
wage_growth_private_yoy.status_note: ABS annual private-sector wage growth, seasonally adjusted; latest observation is 3.1%.

wage_growth_public_yoy.label: Public-sector wage growth, year-on-year
wage_growth_public_yoy.definition: Annual growth in public-sector hourly rates of pay excluding bonuses, seasonally adjusted.
wage_growth_public_yoy.usage: Use it alongside private wages to identify sector differences in household income momentum.
wage_growth_public_yoy.housing_market_link: Public-sector wages support incomes in government-heavy regions and contribute to aggregate serviceability and demand.
wage_growth_public_yoy.status_note: ABS annual public-sector wage growth, seasonally adjusted; latest observation is 3.4%.

average_weekly_earnings_private.label: Private-sector average weekly ordinary earnings
average_weekly_earnings_private.definition: Average weekly ordinary time earnings for private-sector full-time adults, persons, in current dollars and before tax; original series.
average_weekly_earnings_private.usage: Use it as a dollar-level earnings measure. Compare it with WPI because changes can also reflect shifts in workforce composition.
average_weekly_earnings_private.housing_market_link: Higher weekly earnings generally increase borrowing capacity and repayment resilience, although averages do not describe the income distribution.
average_weekly_earnings_private.status_note: ABS original full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings for the private sector; latest value is $2,034.10 per week.
average_weekly_earnings_private.methodology_note: Original six-monthly average. It is affected by workforce composition and is not directly comparable with the fixed-job Wage Price Index.

average_weekly_earnings_public.label: Public-sector average weekly ordinary earnings
average_weekly_earnings_public.definition: Average weekly ordinary time earnings for public-sector full-time adults, persons, in current dollars and before tax; original series.
average_weekly_earnings_public.usage: Use it to compare the dollar level of public-sector earnings with private-sector earnings, allowing for different occupational composition.
average_weekly_earnings_public.housing_market_link: Public-sector earnings can support housing demand in government-employment centres, but this average is not a typical-household income measure.
average_weekly_earnings_public.status_note: ABS original full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings for the public sector; latest value is $2,263.10 per week.
average_weekly_earnings_public.methodology_note: Original six-monthly average. It is affected by workforce composition and is not directly comparable with the fixed-job Wage Price Index.

cpi_nontradables_yoy.label: Non-tradables CPI inflation
cpi_nontradables_yoy.definition: Annual change in the non-tradables component of the Australian CPI.
cpi_nontradables_yoy.usage: Use as a diagnostic for domestically generated and services-heavy inflation persistence.
cpi_nontradables_yoy.housing_market_link: Persistent domestic inflation can delay rate relief and keep mortgage servicing costs elevated.
cpi_nontradables_yoy.status_note: Public RBA series GCPINTIYP; latest published observation is 2026-06 (4.8).
cpi_nontradables_yoy.availability_basis: Pseudo-real-time metadata only: the latest revised historical series is used, with the stated publication lag enforced in forecasting applications.

housing_cpi_yoy.label: CPI housing component inflation
housing_cpi_yoy.definition: Annual change in the CPI housing group, including rents, new dwelling costs and utilities.
housing_cpi_yoy.usage: Track housing-related consumer-price pressure; do not treat it as a dwelling-price index.
housing_cpi_yoy.housing_market_link: Separates housing consumption costs from changes in established-home market values.
housing_cpi_yoy.source: RBA Statistical Table G2 (ABS CPI expenditure groups)
housing_cpi_yoy.status_note: Public RBA series GCPIHOYP; latest published observation is 2026-06 (6.8).
housing_cpi_yoy.availability_basis: Pseudo-real-time metadata only: the latest revised historical series is used, with the stated publication lag enforced in forecasting applications.

consumer_inflation_expectations_1y.label: Consumer inflation expectations (1 year)
consumer_inflation_expectations_1y.definition: Survey measure of consumers' expected inflation over the coming year.
consumer_inflation_expectations_1y.usage: Use as a noisy but timely indicator of household inflation psychology.
consumer_inflation_expectations_1y.housing_market_link: Expectations can affect wage demands, spending and the persistence of restrictive mortgage rates.
consumer_inflation_expectations_1y.status_note: Public RBA series GCONEXP; latest published observation is 2026-06 (5.5).
consumer_inflation_expectations_1y.availability_basis: Pseudo-real-time metadata only: the latest revised historical series is used, with the stated publication lag enforced in forecasting applications.

market_economist_inflation_expectations_.label: Market economists' inflation expectations (1 year)
market_economist_inflation_expectations_.definition: Survey expectation of CPI inflation from market economists at a one-year horizon.
market_economist_inflation_expectations_.usage: Compare professional expectations with consumer expectations and market pricing.
market_economist_inflation_expectations_.housing_market_link: Affects the expected policy path and therefore fixed and variable housing finance conditions.
market_economist_inflation_expectations_.status_note: Public RBA series GMAREXPY; latest published observation is 2026-09 (3.0).
market_economist_inflation_expectations_.availability_basis: Pseudo-real-time metadata only: the latest revised historical series is used, with the stated publication lag enforced in forecasting applications.

market_economist_inflation_expectations_.label: Market economists' inflation expectations (2 years)
market_economist_inflation_expectations_.definition: Survey expectation of CPI inflation from market economists at a two-year horizon.
market_economist_inflation_expectations_.usage: Assess whether inflation expectations are converging toward the RBA target over the policy horizon.
market_economist_inflation_expectations_.housing_market_link: Anchored medium-term expectations support eventual mortgage-rate normalisation.
market_economist_inflation_expectations_.status_note: Public RBA series GMAREXPYY; latest published observation is 2026-09 (2.5).
market_economist_inflation_expectations_.availability_basis: Pseudo-real-time metadata only: the latest revised historical series is used, with the stated publication lag enforced in forecasting applications.

breakeven_inflation_10y.label: 10-year bond breakeven inflation
breakeven_inflation_10y.definition: RBA-published difference between nominal and indexed Australian government bond yields at a long horizon.
breakeven_inflation_10y.usage: Use as a market-based inflation-compensation proxy, not a pure expectation; liquidity and risk premia matter.
breakeven_inflation_10y.housing_market_link: Long-run inflation compensation influences nominal bond yields and fixed mortgage pricing.
breakeven_inflation_10y.methodology_note: Breakeven inflation combines expected inflation with inflation-risk and liquidity premia; it must not be interpreted as a pure inflation forecast.
breakeven_inflation_10y.status_note: Public RBA series GBONYLD; latest published observation is 2026-06 (2.3).
breakeven_inflation_10y.availability_basis: Pseudo-real-time metadata only: the latest revised historical series is used, with the stated publication lag enforced in forecasting applications.

wage_growth_total_yoy.label: Wage Price Index growth
wage_growth_total_yoy.definition: Annual growth in the Australian Wage Price Index across all sectors.
wage_growth_total_yoy.usage: Use as the broad fixed-job wage-pressure measure alongside sector-specific WPI series.
wage_growth_total_yoy.housing_market_link: Wage growth supports borrowing capacity but may prolong inflation and high mortgage rates.

wage_growth_total_yoy.availability_basis: Pseudo-real-time metadata only: the latest revised historical series is used, with the stated publication lag enforced in forecasting applications.

unit_labour_costs_yoy.label: Nominal unit labour cost growth
unit_labour_costs_yoy.definition: Annual growth in nominal non-farm unit labour costs.
unit_labour_costs_yoy.usage: Assess wage pressure relative to productivity rather than wages in isolation.
unit_labour_costs_yoy.housing_market_link: Persistent labour-cost pressure can slow disinflation and delay reductions in housing finance costs.
unit_labour_costs_yoy.source: RBA Statistical Table H4 (Labour Costs and Productivity)

unit_labour_costs_yoy.availability_basis: Pseudo-real-time metadata only: the latest revised historical series is used, with the stated publication lag enforced in forecasting applications.

labour_productivity_yoy.label: Labour productivity growth
labour_productivity_yoy.definition: Annual growth in non-farm GDP per hour worked.
labour_productivity_yoy.usage: Interpret whether wage growth is inflationary or supported by productivity gains.
labour_productivity_yoy.housing_market_link: Stronger productivity can support real incomes and lower inflation pressure over time.
labour_productivity_yoy.source: RBA Statistical Table H4 (Labour Costs and Productivity)
labour_productivity_yoy.status_note: Public RBA series GNFPROSQP; latest published observation is 2026-03 (0.1).
labour_productivity_yoy.availability_basis: Pseudo-real-time metadata only: the latest revised historical series is used, with the stated publication lag enforced in forecasting applications.

real_gdp_growth_yoy.usage: Track aggregate economic momentum and recession risk.
real_gdp_growth_yoy.housing_market_link: Growth affects employment, household income, credit demand and arrears risk.

real_gdp_per_capita_growth_yoy.usage: Distinguish population-led aggregate growth from changes in average economic activity.

business_conditions.label: NAB business conditions index
business_conditions.definition: NAB business conditions index republished by the RBA.

house_price_nominal_index.label: Australian residential property prices (nominal)
house_price_nominal_index.definition: BIS selected nominal residential property price index for Australia, covering the longest available linked history.
house_price_nominal_index.usage: Use it as the primary long-run housing-cycle measure and as a target variable for national backtests.
house_price_nominal_index.housing_market_link: It measures the long-run level and cycle of Australian dwelling prices, but its historical coverage and property definitions change at documented break points.
house_price_nominal_index.methodology_note: Linked BIS history: state-capital median prices to 1986 Q2, detached houses in eight cities to 2003 Q2, all dwellings in eight cities to 2021 Q4, and national all-dwelling coverage thereafter. Do not interpret the joins as a single unchanged hedonic sample.
house_price_nominal_index.status_note: BIS selected series retrieved through FRED; linked history contains documented coverage and methodology breaks.

house_price_real_index.label: Australian residential property prices (real)
house_price_real_index.definition: BIS selected residential property price index for Australia deflated by consumer prices.
house_price_real_index.usage: Use it to distinguish real housing wealth cycles from movements that merely reflect general inflation.
house_price_real_index.housing_market_link: Sustained real price increases indicate housing values outpacing consumer prices and can signal valuation and affordability pressure.
house_price_real_index.methodology_note: Linked BIS history: state-capital median prices to 1986 Q2, detached houses in eight cities to 2003 Q2, all dwellings in eight cities to 2021 Q4, and national all-dwelling coverage thereafter. Do not interpret the joins as a single unchanged hedonic sample.
house_price_real_index.status_note: BIS selected series retrieved through FRED; linked history contains documented coverage and methodology breaks.

household_debt_to_income.label: Household debt to disposable income
household_debt_to_income.definition: Total household debt as a percentage of annualised household disposable income.
household_debt_to_income.usage: Use it as a stock measure of household leverage and sensitivity to income or interest-rate shocks.
household_debt_to_income.housing_market_link: Higher leverage can amplify both housing upswings and the cash-flow effect of mortgage-rate increases.
household_debt_to_income.methodology_note: Latest revised history; use release-lag metadata in pseudo-real-time backtests.
household_debt_to_income.status_note: Public RBA series BHFDDIT; latest revised observation is 2026-Q1.

housing_debt_to_income.label: Housing debt to disposable income
housing_debt_to_income.definition: Household housing debt as a percentage of annualised household disposable income.
housing_debt_to_income.usage: Use it to isolate mortgage-related leverage from other household borrowing.
housing_debt_to_income.housing_market_link: It captures the debt stock most directly connected to dwelling purchases and mortgage serviceability.
housing_debt_to_income.methodology_note: Latest revised history; use release-lag metadata in pseudo-real-time backtests.
housing_debt_to_income.status_note: Public RBA series BHFDDIH; latest revised observation is 2026-Q1.

owner_occupier_housing_debt_to_income.label: Owner-occupier housing debt to disposable income
owner_occupier_housing_debt_to_income.definition: Seasonally adjusted owner-occupier housing debt as a percentage of annualised household disposable income.
owner_occupier_housing_debt_to_income.usage: Use it to track leverage associated with owner-occupied rather than investor housing debt.
owner_occupier_housing_debt_to_income.housing_market_link: It indicates how exposed owner-occupier household balance sheets are to mortgage rates and income shocks.
owner_occupier_housing_debt_to_income.methodology_note: Latest revised history; use release-lag metadata in pseudo-real-time backtests.
owner_occupier_housing_debt_to_income.status_note: Public RBA series BHFDDIO; latest revised observation is 2026-Q1.

housing_interest_charged_to_income.label: Housing interest charged to disposable income
housing_interest_charged_to_income.definition: Interest charged on total housing loans relative to household disposable income.
housing_interest_charged_to_income.usage: Use it as a direct interest-burden measure rather than relying only on mortgage rates or debt stocks.
housing_interest_charged_to_income.housing_market_link: A rising ratio reduces household free cash flow and can weaken purchasing capacity and discretionary consumption.
housing_interest_charged_to_income.methodology_note: Latest revised history; use release-lag metadata in pseudo-real-time backtests.
housing_interest_charged_to_income.status_note: Public RBA series LPHTICRI; latest revised observation is 2026-Q1.

scheduled_housing_repayments_to_income.label: Scheduled housing repayments to disposable income
scheduled_housing_repayments_to_income.definition: Scheduled principal and interest repayments on total housing loans relative to household disposable income.
scheduled_housing_repayments_to_income.usage: Use it as the closest aggregate public measure of required mortgage cash-flow pressure.
scheduled_housing_repayments_to_income.housing_market_link: Higher scheduled repayments constrain borrowing capacity and household spending more directly than an interest-only burden measure.
scheduled_housing_repayments_to_income.methodology_note: Latest revised history; use release-lag metadata in pseudo-real-time backtests.
scheduled_housing_repayments_to_income.status_note: Public RBA series LPHTSPRI; latest revised observation is 2026-Q1.

excess_housing_payments_to_income.label: Excess housing payments to disposable income
excess_housing_payments_to_income.definition: Housing-loan payments above scheduled repayments relative to household disposable income.
excess_housing_payments_to_income.usage: Use it as an indicator of voluntary repayment buffers and household balance-sheet resilience.
excess_housing_payments_to_income.housing_market_link: Falling excess payments may show households drawing down repayment buffers as required mortgage costs rise.
excess_housing_payments_to_income.methodology_note: Latest revised history; use release-lag metadata in pseudo-real-time backtests.
excess_housing_payments_to_income.status_note: Public RBA series LPHTEXRI; latest revised observation is 2026-Q1.

dwelling_commencements.label: Dwelling commencements (Australia total; state proxies for cities)
dwelling_commencements.definition: Seasonally adjusted dwelling units commenced across all building types and sectors; city labels display their corresponding state totals.
dwelling_commencements.usage: Use it after approvals to measure projects that actually entered construction, while treating city tabs as state proxies.
dwelling_commencements.housing_market_link: Commencements are a firmer future-supply signal than approvals but still precede completed, occupiable dwellings.
dwelling_commencements.methodology_note: Latest revised history; use release-lag metadata in pseudo-real-time backtests.
dwelling_commencements.status_note: National is Australia. Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth labels are NSW, Victoria, Queensland and Western Australia state proxies.

dwelling_completions.label: Dwelling completions (Australia total; state proxies for cities)
dwelling_completions.definition: Seasonally adjusted completed dwelling units across all building types and sectors; city labels display their corresponding state totals.
dwelling_completions.usage: Use it as the closest standard quarterly measure of newly delivered housing supply.
dwelling_completions.housing_market_link: Completions add usable housing stock and can relieve market pressure when they keep pace with household formation and population growth.
dwelling_completions.methodology_note: Latest revised history; use release-lag metadata in pseudo-real-time backtests.
dwelling_completions.status_note: National is Australia. Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth labels are NSW, Victoria, Queensland and Western Australia state proxies.

estimated_resident_population.label: Estimated resident population (Australia total; state proxies for cities)
estimated_resident_population.definition: ABS estimated resident population; city labels display the corresponding state population rather than capital-city population.
estimated_resident_population.usage: Use state values with state supply measures and the national value with national supply measures.
estimated_resident_population.housing_market_link: Population growth raises potential housing demand, though household formation, age structure and location determine the number and type of dwellings required.
estimated_resident_population.methodology_note: Latest revised history; use release-lag metadata in pseudo-real-time backtests.
estimated_resident_population.source: ABS National, state and territory population
estimated_resident_population.status_note: National is Australia. Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth labels are NSW, Victoria, Queensland and Western Australia state proxies.

net_overseas_migration.label: Net overseas migration (Australia total; state proxies for cities)
net_overseas_migration.definition: Quarterly net overseas migration; city labels display their corresponding state flows.
net_overseas_migration.usage: Use it as a major cyclical driver of population growth, rental demand and initial household formation.
net_overseas_migration.housing_market_link: Migration shocks can affect rental demand quickly and owner-occupier demand later, with impacts varying across states and dwelling types.
net_overseas_migration.methodology_note: Latest revised history; use release-lag metadata in pseudo-real-time backtests.
net_overseas_migration.source: ABS National, state and territory population
net_overseas_migration.status_note: National is Australia. Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth labels are NSW, Victoria, Queensland and Western Australia state proxies.

new_housing_loans_high_dti_share.label: New housing loans with debt-to-income ratio at or above 6x
new_housing_loans_high_dti_share.definition: Share of new owner-occupier and investor housing lending with a debt-to-income ratio of at least six times.
new_housing_loans_high_dti_share.usage: Use it to monitor the riskier tail of new borrower leverage rather than the average borrower.
new_housing_loans_high_dti_share.housing_market_link: A rising high-DTI share can indicate stronger credit-fuelled purchasing capacity and greater sensitivity to income or rate shocks.
new_housing_loans_high_dti_share.methodology_note: Latest revised public history; apply the stated release lag in pseudo-real-time tests.
new_housing_loans_high_dti_share.status_note: Calculated from APRA aggregate ADI property-exposure tables; ratios may change when APRA revises history.

new_housing_loans_high_lvr_share.label: New housing loans with LVR at or above 90%
new_housing_loans_high_lvr_share.definition: Share of new housing term loans with a loan-to-valuation ratio of at least 90%, excluding loans whose LVR was not reported.
new_housing_loans_high_lvr_share.usage: Use it to track the share of new lending with a relatively small borrower equity buffer.
new_housing_loans_high_lvr_share.housing_market_link: High-LVR lending can support marginal buyer demand but leaves borrowers more exposed to price declines and refinancing constraints.
new_housing_loans_high_lvr_share.methodology_note: Latest revised public history; apply the stated release lag in pseudo-real-time tests.
new_housing_loans_high_lvr_share.status_note: Calculated from APRA aggregate ADI property-exposure tables; ratios may change when APRA revises history.

housing_mortgage_non_performing_share.label: Non-performing residential mortgage share
housing_mortgage_non_performing_share.definition: Non-performing residential mortgage loans as a share of total residential mortgage credit outstanding at Australian ADIs.
housing_mortgage_non_performing_share.usage: Use it as an aggregate realised mortgage-stress indicator, while recognising that arrears respond with a lag.
housing_mortgage_non_performing_share.housing_market_link: Rising non-performance can foreshadow lender caution, distressed sales and weaker housing-credit transmission.
housing_mortgage_non_performing_share.methodology_note: Latest revised public history; apply the stated release lag in pseudo-real-time tests.
housing_mortgage_non_performing_share.status_note: Calculated from APRA aggregate ADI property-exposure tables; ratios may change when APRA revises history.

new_housing_loans_interest_only_share.label: Interest-only share of new housing lending
new_housing_loans_interest_only_share.definition: Owner-occupier and investor interest-only new housing loans as a share of new owner-occupier and investor housing lending.
new_housing_loans_interest_only_share.usage: Use it to monitor lending structures that initially defer principal repayment and are often more prevalent among investors.
new_housing_loans_interest_only_share.housing_market_link: A higher share can boost near-term borrowing flexibility but may increase refinancing and repayment-reset risk.
new_housing_loans_interest_only_share.methodology_note: Latest revised public history; apply the stated release lag in pseudo-real-time tests.
new_housing_loans_interest_only_share.status_note: Calculated from APRA aggregate ADI property-exposure tables; ratios may change when APRA revises history.

first_home_buyer_share.label: First-home-buyer share of owner-occupier commitments
first_home_buyer_share.definition: First-home-buyer owner-occupier loan commitments divided by all owner-occupier dwelling loan commitments, by number.
first_home_buyer_share.usage: Use it to assess the composition of financed owner-occupier demand rather than the total level of lending.
first_home_buyer_share.housing_market_link: Changes can reflect affordability, grants, deposit constraints and competition between first and repeat buyers.
first_home_buyer_share.methodology_note: Latest revised public history; apply the stated release lag in pseudo-real-time tests.
first_home_buyer_share.status_note: Calculated from the ABS seasonally adjusted number of new dwelling loan commitments.

investor_lending_share.label: Investor share of new dwelling commitments
investor_lending_share.definition: Investor dwelling loan commitments divided by total new dwelling loan commitments, by number.
investor_lending_share.usage: Use it to measure the investor composition of financed housing demand.
investor_lending_share.housing_market_link: Investor participation can affect apartment demand, rental supply and the sensitivity of market activity to tax and credit policy.
investor_lending_share.methodology_note: Latest revised public history; apply the stated release lag in pseudo-real-time tests.
investor_lending_share.status_note: Calculated from the ABS seasonally adjusted number of new dwelling loan commitments.

capital_city_rent_index.label: Consumer rent index by capital city
capital_city_rent_index.definition: ABS CPI rents index for the weighted average of eight capital cities and for Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth.
capital_city_rent_index.usage: Use it to compare the direction and pace of advertised-and-existing tenancy rent inflation across capital cities.
capital_city_rent_index.housing_market_link: Rent growth is a direct signal of housing scarcity and affects investor yields, affordability and the rent-versus-buy decision.
capital_city_rent_index.methodology_note: ABS introduced complete monthly CPI publication and a new rents data source from July 2022. This series deliberately avoids mechanically splicing differently referenced older quarterly indexes.
capital_city_rent_index.status_note: Official monthly rents indexes. The current monthly methodology begins in July 2022 and is referenced to September 2025=100.

residential_property_transfers.label: Residential property transfers by capital city
residential_property_transfers.definition: Number of established-house and attached-dwelling transfers in each capital city; National is the sum of the eight published capital cities.
residential_property_transfers.usage: Use it as a settled transaction-volume measure rather than an advertised-listing or finance-approval measure.
residential_property_transfers.housing_market_link: Turnover tends to weaken when credit conditions tighten and strengthen as confidence and market liquidity recover.
residential_property_transfers.methodology_note: Latest revised public history; apply the stated release lag in pseudo-real-time tests.
residential_property_transfers.status_note: Established-house plus attached-dwelling transfers. National is the sum of the eight published capital cities.

residential_dwelling_stock.label: Estimated residential dwelling stock (Australia total; state proxies for cities)
residential_dwelling_stock.definition: ABS estimated number of residential dwellings; city-labelled views use NSW, Victoria, Queensland and Western Australia as state proxies.
residential_dwelling_stock.usage: Use it as the denominator for supply, turnover and population-per-dwelling indicators, keeping the proxy geography explicit.
residential_dwelling_stock.housing_market_link: The stock grows slowly, so demand shocks can produce large rent and price effects when additions lag household formation.
residential_dwelling_stock.methodology_note: Latest revised public history; apply the stated release lag in pseudo-real-time tests.
residential_dwelling_stock.status_note: National is Australia; city labels are state proxies (NSW, Victoria, Queensland and Western Australia).

capital_city_population_growth.label: Capital-city population growth
capital_city_population_growth.definition: Annual growth in estimated resident population for Greater Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth; National combines all eight Greater Capital City Statistical Areas.
capital_city_population_growth.usage: Use it with capital-city rents, transfers and supply indicators to compare demand pressure across metropolitan markets.
capital_city_population_growth.housing_market_link: Population growth raises housing demand, but dwelling requirements also depend on household size, age structure and vacancy rates.
capital_city_population_growth.methodology_note: Latest revised public history; apply the stated release lag in pseudo-real-time tests.
capital_city_population_growth.status_note: Growth calculated from annual GCCSA estimated resident population. National combines the eight greater capital cities.

real_cash_rate_trimmed_mean.label: Real cash rate (trimmed mean basis)
real_cash_rate_trimmed_mean.definition: An ex-post real policy-rate proxy, expressed as the cash rate less underlying annual inflation.
real_cash_rate_trimmed_mean.usage: Read positive values as restrictive in real terms and negative values as accommodative, while allowing for the backward-looking inflation denominator.
real_cash_rate_trimmed_mean.housing_market_link: Higher real policy rates generally weaken borrowing capacity and housing demand; easing real rates can improve financing conditions.
real_cash_rate_trimmed_mean.source: Calculated from Reserve Bank of Australia and ABS Consumer Price Index, Australia
real_cash_rate_trimmed_mean.calculation: RBA cash rate target minus annual trimmed mean CPI inflation
real_cash_rate_trimmed_mean.methodology_note: The cash rate is carried to each CPI observation period. This is an analytical proxy, not an expected real rate.

real_mortgage_rate_headline.label: Real variable mortgage rate
real_mortgage_rate_headline.definition: An ex-post real mortgage-rate proxy using the average outstanding owner-occupier variable lending rate.
real_mortgage_rate_headline.usage: Use it to compare nominal mortgage pricing with realised inflation, not as a direct household cash-flow measure.
real_mortgage_rate_headline.housing_market_link: A rising real mortgage rate increases the inflation-adjusted financing hurdle facing leveraged buyers and existing borrowers.
real_mortgage_rate_headline.source: Calculated from RBA Housing Lending Rates (F6) and ABS Consumer Price Index, Australia
real_mortgage_rate_headline.calculation: Owner-occupier variable mortgage rate minus annual headline CPI inflation
real_mortgage_rate_headline.methodology_note: The latest CPI observation at or before each mortgage-rate month is used. Borrower-specific rates differ from this system average.

mortgage_cash_spread.label: Variable mortgage rate spread to cash rate
mortgage_cash_spread.definition: The gap between the average outstanding variable owner-occupier mortgage rate and the policy cash rate.
mortgage_cash_spread.usage: Track whether lender pricing is amplifying or cushioning changes in the policy rate.
mortgage_cash_spread.housing_market_link: A wider spread tightens household financing conditions beyond the cash-rate setting; a narrower spread provides some offset.
mortgage_cash_spread.source: Calculated from RBA Housing Lending Rates (F6) and Reserve Bank of Australia
mortgage_cash_spread.calculation: Owner-occupier variable mortgage rate minus RBA cash rate target
mortgage_cash_spread.methodology_note: The latest cash-rate setting in each mortgage-rate month is used.

real_wage_growth_private.label: Real private-sector wage growth
real_wage_growth_private.definition: A purchasing-power proxy for private-sector wages after headline consumer-price inflation.
real_wage_growth_private.usage: Use the sign and direction to assess whether wage growth is gaining or losing ground against consumer prices.
real_wage_growth_private.housing_market_link: Sustained positive real wage growth can improve deposit accumulation and mortgage serviceability; negative growth can constrain both.
real_wage_growth_private.source: Calculated from ABS Wage Price Index, Australia and ABS Consumer Price Index, Australia
real_wage_growth_private.calculation: Annual private-sector Wage Price Index growth minus annual headline CPI inflation
real_wage_growth_private.methodology_note: The latest CPI observation at or before each wage quarter is used. This is a growth differential, not a household-income level.

real_wage_growth_public.label: Real public-sector wage growth
real_wage_growth_public.definition: A purchasing-power proxy for public-sector wages after headline consumer-price inflation.
real_wage_growth_public.usage: Use the sign and direction to assess whether wage growth is gaining or losing ground against consumer prices.
real_wage_growth_public.housing_market_link: Sustained positive real wage growth can improve deposit accumulation and mortgage serviceability; negative growth can constrain both.
real_wage_growth_public.source: Calculated from ABS Wage Price Index, Australia and ABS Consumer Price Index, Australia
real_wage_growth_public.calculation: Annual public-sector Wage Price Index growth minus annual headline CPI inflation
real_wage_growth_public.methodology_note: The latest CPI observation at or before each wage quarter is used. This is a growth differential, not a household-income level.

us_yield_curve_10y_3y.label: US Treasury 10-year minus 3-year spread
us_yield_curve_10y_3y.definition: A medium-to-long US yield-curve slope measure; negative readings indicate inversion between these maturities.
us_yield_curve_10y_3y.usage: Use it as a global growth and rate-cycle signal rather than a direct Australian mortgage-rate forecast.
us_yield_curve_10y_3y.housing_market_link: Global bond conditions influence Australian wholesale funding and longer-term discount rates, indirectly affecting lenders and property assets.
us_yield_curve_10y_3y.source: Calculated from Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED DGS10) and Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED DGS3)

component_sources.name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED DGS10)
Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED DGS3)

us_yield_curve_10y_3y.calculation: US 10-year Treasury yield minus US 3-year Treasury yield
us_yield_curve_10y_3y.methodology_note: Calculated from matched monthly FRED observations.

average_new_dwelling_loan_value.label: Implied average new dwelling loan commitment
average_new_dwelling_loan_value.definition: The implied average dollar value per new dwelling loan commitment in the ABS aggregate data.
average_new_dwelling_loan_value.usage: Use it to track changes in the typical financed amount, while remembering that shifts in borrower and dwelling mix also move the average.
average_new_dwelling_loan_value.housing_market_link: Rising average commitments may signal higher prices, larger deposits, stronger borrowing capacity, or a shift toward more expensive markets.
average_new_dwelling_loan_value.calculation: Total value of new dwelling loan commitments divided by total number of commitments
average_new_dwelling_loan_value.methodology_note: Aggregate value divided by aggregate count. It is not the ABS median loan size and excludes refinancing consistently with the inputs.

housing_turnover_rate.label: Capital-city housing turnover rate proxy
housing_turnover_rate.definition: Capital-city residential transfers expressed as a share of the Australia-wide dwelling stock during each quarter.
housing_turnover_rate.usage: Use it as a broad market-liquidity and transaction-intensity measure; compare the same quarter across years to allow for seasonality.
housing_turnover_rate.housing_market_link: Higher turnover generally accompanies stronger buyer-seller matching and market activity, while low turnover can signal affordability or financing constraints.
housing_turnover_rate.source: Calculated from ABS Total Value of Dwellings
housing_turnover_rate.calculation: Residential property transfers divided by estimated residential dwelling stock, multiplied by 100
housing_turnover_rate.methodology_note: The numerator sums eight capital cities while the available denominator is Australia-wide dwelling stock, so the level understates a like-for-like capital-city turnover rate. It is not annualised and can include transfers that are not ordinary arm's-length sales.

price_to_rent_ratio_proxy.label: House price-to-rent ratio proxy
price_to_rent_ratio_proxy.definition: A relative valuation proxy comparing national dwelling prices with capital-city rents.
price_to_rent_ratio_proxy.usage: Use changes and turning points rather than the absolute level because the two source indexes have different bases and geographic coverage.
price_to_rent_ratio_proxy.housing_market_link: A rising ratio means purchase prices are increasing faster than rents, often implying lower gross rental yield and greater valuation sensitivity to financing costs.
price_to_rent_ratio_proxy.source: Calculated from Bank for International Settlements (via FRED) and ABS Consumer Price Index, Australia
price_to_rent_ratio_proxy.calculation: BIS nominal house-price index divided by the ABS capital-city rent index, rebased to 100 at the first common period
price_to_rent_ratio_proxy.methodology_note: The latest quarterly house-price observation is carried to each monthly rent observation. This is an indexed proxy, not a dollar price-to-annual-rent multiple.

average_loan_to_income_proxy.label: Average new loan-to-income proxy
average_loan_to_income_proxy.definition: A borrowing-size proxy comparing the average new dwelling commitment with one annual private-sector wage.
average_loan_to_income_proxy.usage: Track direction rather than interpreting it as a regulated borrower DTI: household loans may have multiple incomes and the earnings denominator is an economy-wide average.
average_loan_to_income_proxy.housing_market_link: A rising multiple can indicate that financed dwelling purchases are stretching further relative to wage income.
average_loan_to_income_proxy.source: Calculated from ABS Lending Indicators and ABS Average Weekly Earnings, Australia
average_loan_to_income_proxy.calculation: Implied average new dwelling loan divided by 52 times private-sector average weekly ordinary-time earnings
average_loan_to_income_proxy.methodology_note: The latest available semiannual earnings observation is carried to each lending quarter. This is not household disposable income and is not an individual loan-serviceability measure.

mortgage_credit_quality_risk_index.label: Mortgage credit-quality risk index
mortgage_credit_quality_risk_index.definition: A transparent composite of riskier new-lending composition and realised mortgage non-performance.
mortgage_credit_quality_risk_index.usage: Positive values indicate higher measured credit risk than the history available at that date; inspect the four components before drawing conclusions.
mortgage_credit_quality_risk_index.housing_market_link: Looser origination composition can support near-term demand but may increase later household and lender vulnerability, while non-performance is usually a lagging stress signal.
mortgage_credit_quality_risk_index.source: Calculated from APRA Quarterly ADI Property Exposures
mortgage_credit_quality_risk_index.calculation: Equal average of expanding z-scores for high-DTI, high-LVR, interest-only and non-performing mortgage shares
mortgage_credit_quality_risk_index.methodology_note: All inputs are sign-aligned so higher means riskier, shifted by an estimated three-month release lag and standardised using expanding history only.

dwelling_completions_per_1000_population.label: Dwelling completions per 1,000 population
dwelling_completions_per_1000_population.definition: The annual flow of completed dwellings scaled by population.
dwelling_completions_per_1000_population.usage: Use it to compare supply delivery through time without allowing population size alone to dominate the count.
dwelling_completions_per_1000_population.housing_market_link: Persistently low completions per capita can intensify housing scarcity when household formation and migration remain strong.
dwelling_completions_per_1000_population.source: Calculated from ABS Building Activity, Australia and ABS National, state and territory population

component_sources.name: ABS National, state and territory population

dwelling_completions_per_1000_population.calculation: Trailing four-quarter dwelling completions divided by estimated resident population, multiplied by 1,000
dwelling_completions_per_1000_population.methodology_note: Population is matched as of each completion quarter. State/city extensions should retain the existing state-proxy labels.

estimated_housing_demand_gap.label: Estimated housing demand less completions
estimated_housing_demand_gap.definition: A simple demographic-demand-minus-new-supply gap expressed as an estimated number of dwellings.
estimated_housing_demand_gap.usage: Treat it as a scenario indicator, not a forecast: household size, vacancies, demolitions and internal migration can materially change realised demand.
estimated_housing_demand_gap.housing_market_link: A positive gap suggests population-implied household formation is running ahead of completions, which can add pressure to rents and prices if sustained.
estimated_housing_demand_gap.source: Calculated from ABS National, state and territory population and ABS Building Activity, Australia

component_sources.name: ABS National, state and territory population

estimated_housing_demand_gap.calculation: Annual population increase divided by an assumed 2.5 persons per dwelling, minus trailing four-quarter dwelling completions
estimated_housing_demand_gap.methodology_note: Uses a fixed 2.5 persons-per-dwelling assumption for transparency. Future work should replace it with household-formation projections and account for demolitions and vacant stock.

first_home_buyer_credit_impulse.label: First-home-buyer commitment impulse proxy
first_home_buyer_credit_impulse.definition: A commitment-acceleration proxy for the selected borrower segment; positive values mean annual loan-count growth is accelerating.
first_home_buyer_credit_impulse.usage: Use it to identify changes in segment momentum, not the level of credit supplied or a structural estimate of demand.
first_home_buyer_credit_impulse.housing_market_link: A positive impulse can precede stronger buyer competition from that segment, while a negative impulse indicates fading lending momentum.
first_home_buyer_credit_impulse.calculation: Annual growth in imputed segment commitment count (total commitment count times the estimated owner-occupier share times the first-home-buyer share) minus its annual growth rate four quarters earlier
first_home_buyer_credit_impulse.methodology_note: Segment counts are imputed from aggregate commitment counts and published count shares. The impulse is the annual change in the segment's year-on-year growth rate, not a dollar credit-flow measure.

investor_credit_impulse.label: Investor commitment impulse proxy
investor_credit_impulse.definition: A commitment-acceleration proxy for the selected borrower segment; positive values mean annual loan-count growth is accelerating.
investor_credit_impulse.usage: Use it to identify changes in segment momentum, not the level of credit supplied or a structural estimate of demand.
investor_credit_impulse.housing_market_link: A positive impulse can precede stronger buyer competition from that segment, while a negative impulse indicates fading lending momentum.
investor_credit_impulse.calculation: Annual growth in imputed segment commitment count (total commitment count times the investor share) minus its annual growth rate four quarters earlier
investor_credit_impulse.methodology_note: Segment counts are imputed from aggregate commitment counts and published count shares. The impulse is the annual change in the segment's year-on-year growth rate, not a dollar credit-flow measure.

dwelling_approvals_yoy.label: Dwelling approvals annual growth
dwelling_approvals_yoy.definition: The annual growth rate of total seasonally adjusted Australian dwelling approvals.
dwelling_approvals_yoy.usage: Use it to identify acceleration or contraction in the prospective residential construction pipeline while looking through monthly volatility.
dwelling_approvals_yoy.housing_market_link: Stronger approvals growth points to a potentially larger future supply pipeline, although approvals do not always translate into commencements or completions.
dwelling_approvals_yoy.source: Calculated from ABS Building Approvals, Australia
dwelling_approvals_yoy.calculation: Percentage change in seasonally adjusted dwelling approvals from 12 months earlier
dwelling_approvals_yoy.methodology_note: Calculated only where an observation exists exactly 12 months earlier.

asx_real_estate_relative.label: ASX 200 Real Estate relative to ASX 200
asx_real_estate_relative.definition: A relative-price index showing whether listed real-estate exposure has outperformed or underperformed the broad Australian equity market.
asx_real_estate_relative.usage: Values above 100 indicate cumulative outperformance since the common start; focus on direction and cycles rather than the absolute level.
asx_real_estate_relative.housing_market_link: Relative performance captures market expectations for property earnings, funding costs and valuations, but listed exposures are not a direct measure of dwelling prices.
asx_real_estate_relative.source: Calculated from S&P/ASX 200 Real Estate Index and S&P/ASX 200
asx_real_estate_relative.calculation: Ratio of S&P/ASX 200 Real Estate Index to S&P/ASX 200, rebased to 100 at the first common month
asx_real_estate_relative.methodology_note: Monthly price-index levels are divided and rebased. Dividends are excluded where the component series is a price-return index.

asx_areit_relative.label: ASX 200 A-REIT relative to ASX 200
asx_areit_relative.definition: A relative-price index showing whether listed real-estate exposure has outperformed or underperformed the broad Australian equity market.
asx_areit_relative.usage: Values above 100 indicate cumulative outperformance since the common start; focus on direction and cycles rather than the absolute level.
asx_areit_relative.housing_market_link: Relative performance captures market expectations for property earnings, funding costs and valuations, but listed exposures are not a direct measure of dwelling prices.
asx_areit_relative.source: Calculated from S&P/ASX 200 A-REIT Index and S&P/ASX 200
asx_areit_relative.calculation: Ratio of S&P/ASX 200 A-REIT Index to S&P/ASX 200, rebased to 100 at the first common month
asx_areit_relative.methodology_note: Monthly price-index levels are divided and rebased. Dividends are excluded where the component series is a price-return index.

hfci_core.label: Core Housing Financial Conditions Index
hfci_core.definition: A financial-price index combining real policy and mortgage rates, the mortgage spread, government and BBB yields, and listed real-estate relative performance.
hfci_core.usage: Use it as the comparatively pure financing-price benchmark, excluding credit quantities, employment and wages.
hfci_core.housing_market_link: Positive readings indicate tighter-than-history housing financial conditions; negative readings indicate easier conditions. Use turning points and block contributions rather than treating the level as a causal estimate.
hfci_core.source: Calculated from S&P/ASX 200 and S&P/ASX 200 A-REIT Index and RBA Statistical Table F17 (Indicative Mid Rates of Australian Government Securities) and Reserve Bank of Australia and RBA Statistical Table F3 (Aggregate Measures of Australian Corporate Bond Yields) and ABS Consumer Price Index, Australia and RBA Statistical Table F6 (Housing Lending Rates)

RBA Statistical Table F3 (Aggregate Measures of Australian Corporate Bond Yields)

hfci_core.calculation: 50% Pricing block and 50% Market Pricing block
hfci_core.methodology_note: Each input is sign-aligned, shifted by its estimated publication lag and standardised using only its expanding history. Variables are equally weighted within blocks and blocks are equally weighted. Complete block composition is required; the index is a transparent research indicator, not an official measure or causal estimate.
